name: mantis
description: A Scala based client for Ethereum-like Blockchains.

documents.title: Introducción
documents.text: Mantis Ethereum-like Blockchain Scala client built by IOHK's for Ethereum Classic (ETC) network

documents.title: Status - Not maintained
documents.text: The lastest ETC hard-fork supported by the client is Magneto hard-fork You can check the latest build results of the current branch by clicking the status icon in the header of the Github file browser.

documents.title: Command line version
documents.text: In the bin directory, you can find the generic launcher. To connect to a pre-configured network just pass the network name as a parameter. Example: - ./bin/mantis-launcher etc - for joining Ethereum Classic network Possible networks: etc , eth , mordor , testnet-internal

documents.title: Command Line Interface
documents.text: cli is a tool that can be used to: - generate a new private key - derive an address from private key - generate genesis allocs (using private keys and/or addresses) - generate multiple key-pairs (following example generate 5 key-pairs) - encrypt private key (default passphrase is empty string) The command output uses the same format as the keystore so it could be used ex. to setup private faucet ex.

documents.title: Prerequisites to build
documents.text: - JDK 1.8 (download from java.com) - sbt (download sbt) - python 2.7.15 (download from python.org)

documents.title: Build the client
documents.text: In the root of the project: This updates all submodules and creates a distribution zip in ~/target/universal/ . Note: building in dev mode allows faster and incremental compilation, for this: - set environment variable MANTIS DEV to true , or - use the system property -DmantisDev=true

documents.title: On a Mac
documents.text: This project uses Nix for CI, deployment and, optionally, local development. Some of the dependencies are not available for Darwin (macOS) however. To work with Nix on a Mac you can instead use Docker via the nix-in-docker/run script, which will start a nix-shell with the same environment as CI.

documents.title: Update sbt+nix dependencies
documents.text: When updating project dependencies, the nix fixed-output-derivation will need to be updated so that it includes the new dependency state. To do so, please run: For this command to work you'll need the Flakes feature enabled in your nix environment. NOTE: This should only be necessary when updating dependencies (For example, edits to build.sbt or project/plugins.sbt will likely need to be regenerated)

documents.title: Locally build & run monitoring client
documents.text: A docker-compose setup using Prometheus and Grafana, and a preconfigured dashboard, is available. As a precondition you need to have docker and sbt installed. Before running the script, you need to enable metrics by editing the file metrics.conf and setting mantis.metrics.enabled=true To build the monitoring, run the following script at ./docker/mantis/build.sh . This script builds a docker image of mantis using the local sources and starts the docker-compose. Grafana will be available at http://localhost:3000 (using user and password: admin and admin) with a dashboard called Mantis .

documents.title: TLS setup
documents.text: Both the JSON RPC (on the node and faucet) can be additionally protected using TLS. The development environment it already properly configured with a development certificate.

documents.title: Generating a new certificate
documents.text: If a new certificate is required, create a new keystore with a certificate by running ./tls/gen-cert.sh

documents.title: Configuring the node
documents.text: 1. Configure the certificate and password file to be used at mantis.network.rpc.http.certificate key on the application.conf file: keystore-path: path to the keystore storing the certificates (if generated through our script they are by default located in "./tls/mantisCA.p12") keystore-type: type of certificate keystore being used (if generated through our script use "pkcs12") password-file: path to the file with the password used for accessing the certificate keystore (if generated through our script they are by default located in "./tls/password") 2. Enable TLS in specific config: - For JSON RPC: mantis.network.rpc.http.mode=https

documents.title: Configuring the faucet
documents.text: 1. Configure the certificate and password file to be used at mantis.network.rpc.http.certificate key on the faucet.conf file: keystore-path: path to the keystore storing the certificates (if generated through our script they are by default located in "./tls/mantisCA.p12") keystore-type: type of certificate keystore being used (if generated through our script use "pkcs12") password-file: path to the file with the password used for accessing the certificate keystore (if generated through our script they are by default located in "./tls/password") 2. Enable TLS in specific config: - For JSON RPC: mantis.network.rpc.http.mode=https 3. Configure the certificate used from RpcClient to connect with the node. Necessary if the node uses http secure. This certificate and password file to be used at faucet.rpc-client.certificate key on the faucet.conf file: keystore-path: path to the keystore storing the certificates keystore-type: type of certificate keystore being used (if generated through our script use "pkcs12") password-file: path to the file with the password used for accessing the certificate keystore

Now check the keystore folder in ~/.mantis/testnet-internal-nomad/keystore . Inside you will find a key generate with the curl request sent in step 2. . Copy that file to ~/.mantis-faucet/keystore/ : 5. Start the faucet in command line: 6. Run the following curl command to send tokens from your faucet to a wallet address: Happy transfer!
